title: 04. OOP: ABSTRACT BASE CLASSES & PROTOCOLS
summary: ABSTRACT BASE CLASSES & PROTOCOLS: Not inheriting from Drawable — but still conforms!; ABC vs PROTOCOL — Two approaches to interfaces in Python.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.body:
```python name=advanced/abc_protocols.py
# ============================================================
# ABC vs PROTOCOL — Two approaches to interfaces in Python
# ============================================================
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

# ============================================================
# ABC — Nominal Typing (explicit inheritance)
# ============================================================
# "You MUST inherit from this class to be accepted."

class Serializable(ABC):
    @abstractmethod
    def serialize(self) -> str: ...
    
    @abstractmethod
    def deserialize(self, data: str) -> None: ...
    
    # Can have concrete methods too!
    def to_file(self, filepath: str):
        with open(filepath, "w") as f:
            f.write(self.serialize())

class User(Serializable):  # MUST inherit explicitly
    def __init__(self, name: str):
        self.name = name
    
    def serialize(self) -> str:
        return f'{{"name": "{self.name}"}}'
    
    def deserialize(self, data: str):
        import json
        self.name = json.loads(data)["name"]

# ============================================================
# PROTOCOL — Structural Typing (duck typing with type checking)
# ============================================================
# "You just need to have these methods. No inheritance needed."

@runtime_checkable
class Drawable(Protocol):
    def draw(self) -> None: ...
    def resize(self, factor: float) -> None: ...

class Circle:
    """Not inheriting from Drawable — but still conforms!"""
    def draw(self):
        print("Drawing circle")
    def resize(self, factor):
        print(f"Resizing by {factor}")

class Square:
    def draw(self):
        print("Drawing square")
    def resize(self, factor):
        print(f"Resizing by {factor}")

def render(shape: Drawable):  # Accepts anything with draw() and resize()
    shape.draw()

render(Circle())   # Works!
render(Square())   # Works!
print(isinstance(Circle(), Drawable))  # True (with @runtime_checkable)

# ============================================================
# WHEN TO USE WHICH?
# ============================================================
# ABC:
#   - When you want to FORCE inheritance
#   - When you provide shared concrete methods
#   - When you want strict type hierarchy
#   - Example: Framework base classes
#
# Protocol:
#   - When you want duck typing with type safety
#   - When classes come from third-party libraries (can't modify)
#   - When you want loose coupling
#   - Example: Anything that's "something-able" (Drawable, Sortable)

# --- Abstract Properties ---
class Shape(ABC):
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def area(self) -> float: ...
    
    @property
    @abstractmethod
    def perimeter(self) -> float: ...

# --- Registering virtual subclasses ---
class MyList:
    def __len__(self): return 0
    def __getitem__(self, i): raise IndexError

from collections.abc import Sequence
Sequence.register(MyList)
print(isinstance(MyList(), Sequence))  # True

# --- Collections ABC hierarchy ---
# collections.abc provides:
# Iterable → __iter__
# Iterator → __iter__ + __next__
# Reversible → __reversed__
# Container → __contains__
# Hashable → __hash__
# Sized → __len__
# Callable → __call__
# Collection → Sized + Iterable + Container
# Sequence → Collection + __getitem__ + __reversed__ + index + count
# MutableSequence → Sequence + __setitem__ + __delitem__ + insert + append + ...
# Set → Collection + set operations
# Mapping → Collection + __getitem__ + keys + values + items
# MutableMapping → Mapping + __setitem__ + __delitem__
```
